title: Workers report findings mechanically, not in prose an orchestrator must read
description:
A worker that discovers something outside its tick has no mechanical way to
report it, so findings are carried in PROSE and depend on an orchestrator
reading carefully. They get lost.

## Observed on this epic alone

Three different shapes, none of them mechanical:

- Tick 604's worker wrote an "UPSTREAM ticks FINDING for the orchestrator to
  file" section into its report. It was filed (ticks tick of9) only because the
  orchestrator happened to read that far. A later reviewer then reported the
  finding as never filed, because it was looking in the cleaned-up worktree
  rather than the archive — a second failure of the same prose channel.
- Tick v3i reported BLOCKED with a four-way split proposed in prose. The
  orchestrator transcribed it by hand into ek7, b3a, 0e1 and 1ya. Correct
  outcome, entirely manual, and it cost a wave slot.
- Tick 8ug wrote an upstream contract finding into its report; it is recorded on
  the tick, but nothing in the tracker will surface it when the bundle is next
  re-pinned.
- Tick 9t0 was filed by a worker DIRECTLY. It is a good tick. It also carries
  `discovered_from: None` — the attempt that found it is already unrecoverable.

## What to build

**1. A typed findings channel in the role-result envelope.**
`RoleResult` (internal/exec/subprocess/record.go:394) already carries
SchemaVersion, SchemaID, Role, Status, Summary, Result, Evidence and Decisions.
It carries no findings. Add a typed list — kind, title, body, severity, and the
target repository, because an upstream finding belongs on a different tracker.
Schema change, so it is a contract-bundle change, pinned the way everything else
in contracts/ is.

**2. Make the reconciler act on it.**
Once findings are typed rather than prose, collect can:
- refuse to CLOSE a tick whose findings have not been triaged, which is what
  stops one falling on the floor;
- stamp every tick created from a finding with the attempt that discovered it,
  so `discovered_from` is never empty again;
- route a finding whose target is another repository to that repository rather
  than dropping it.

**3. Reuse the funnel that already exists.**
ticks already turns declared sources' deliveries into DRAFT TICKS, deduplicated
on `(source, external_ref)`, where a redelivery comes back as a duplicate naming
the original proposal and proposes nothing new — "whatever the human did with
it, including discarding it". That is exactly the shape a worker finding needs,
including the dedup: the same finding WILL recur on every attempt of the same
tick until it is fixed, and a chatty worker must not re-propose something
already declined. Today the funnel accepts webhooks; a worker is simply not a
registered source. See ticks' `skills/ticks/references/runners-config.md` →
"The signal sources a repo accepts".

**4. Draft, not open.**
Workers see real things and they also see scope they want. A DRAFT that an
orchestrator promotes keeps discovery mechanical while keeping the scope
decision human. The 9t0 case shows both halves: a genuinely useful tick, filed
with no provenance and no review.

## Do not

Do not let a worker write the tracker directly. `.tick/` is a protected prefix
for exactly this reason, and tick p6b exists to ENFORCE that boundary rather
than ask for it. The findings channel is how a worker reports; the reconciler is
what writes.
acceptance_criteria: The role-result envelope carries a typed findings list (kind, title, body, severity, target repository), pinned in the contract bundle like every other schema; a worker that reports a finding has it turned into a DRAFT tick by the reconciler, never by the worker writing the tracker itself; every tick created from a finding carries discovered_from naming the attempt; a tick whose findings are untriaged cannot be closed; a finding targeting another repository is routed there rather than dropped; a finding repeated on a later attempt of the same tick is deduplicated against the original proposal and proposes nothing new, including when the original was discarded; tests cover a finding becoming a draft, a repeat being deduplicated, and a close being refused while a finding is untriaged.
closed_reason: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, concern accepted as a residual and routed. Findings now travel as data rather than prose: internal/runstate/findings_store.go plus its tests, with the reconciler turning them into drafts and the dedup the acceptance asked for. The concern is the same upstream boundary 8ug and 5eq both hit — the typed findings list rides in the envelope's OPEN result payload rather than a bundle-pinned first-class field, because contracts/ is byte-verified against the ticks repo and cannot be edited from a worktree. The worker wrote the exact upstream delta out, ready to file. Routed to tick 9t0, which owns the bundle bump. It also reported a pre-existing wait4 hazard under shared-host load and suggested a follow-up. Wave gate green (200.8s).
